text:
Nikita Kucherov asked the Lightning for a trade at the end of October, first reported by Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman, and said publicly that it was about communication and respect, not money. Tampa Bay's general manager answered that the team has no intention of trading him. In the middle of all that he became the franchise's all-time leading scorer, passing Steven Stamkos, and he has kept producing: 28 points in 20 games, including a hat trick in an 8-3 win in Buffalo.

The reigning Hart Trophy winner is on a pace that would be a career year for almost anyone, but not quite his. Last season he had 130 points; this year his points per 60 are down to 3.96 from 5.05, and his own chances have dipped too. Our numbers also say the Lightning have scored 5.7 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, so the 28 points are a little padded. Still, Tampa Bay gets 60% of the expected goals at five-on-five in his minutes, and Evolving-Hockey had him second among all forwards in wins above replacement last season. Whatever happens before the deadline, he's still one of the best players in the world.
